title: [Epic Classic-Style RPG] Does Perfectionism Lead to Going Eternal? ② The Creator's Perspective

blocks.source: 【王道長編RPG】完璧主義はエターなる？② 制作者編
blocks.translation: [Epic Classic-Style RPG] Does Perfectionism Lead to Going Eternal? ② The Creator's Perspective

blocks.source: 完璧主義な制作者
blocks.translation: Perfectionist Creators

blocks.source: さて、前編で終わるつもりだったのですが、そうはいきませんでした。極めて重大な情報が目に入ったためです。それは……
blocks.translation: Well, I intended to wrap things up in the first part, but that didn't happen. I came across some extremely important information. It was this…

blocks.source: 完璧主義者はエターなりやすいということです。
blocks.translation: Perfectionists are prone to going eternal.

blocks.source: ※エターなる：作品を制作途中で放棄することの意。
blocks.translation: ※Going eternal: Abandoning a work while it is still in production.

blocks.source: ……この情報には僕も驚愕を隠せません。完璧主義者はプレイヤーとしては、アイテムコンプのような地道な作業を完遂できる性質を持っています。相当な根気強さを持っているため、どちらかというと、完成できるタイプなのだと考えていました。
blocks.translation: …I can't hide my astonishment at this information either. As players, perfectionists have the disposition to complete painstaking tasks such as collecting every item. Since they possess considerable perseverance, I had thought they were, if anything, the type who could finish things.

blocks.source: それがなぜ、エターなるというのか？ これは「人はなぜエターなるのか？」という命題を追求してきた僕としては看過できません。エターナルのメカニズムを解き明かし、より多くのエターナラーをエターナルの海から救出することこそが、ＲＰＧ制作講座の至上命題といっても過言ではありません。
blocks.translation: Why, then, do they go eternal? As someone who has pursued the question “Why do people go eternal?”, I can't overlook this. It would not be an exaggeration to say that unraveling the mechanism of going eternal and rescuing as many eternalizers as possible from the sea of eternity is the supreme mission of [RPG Design Guides] .

blocks.source: というわけで、徹底調査しました。完璧主義者の心理についてはかなり豊富な調査結果があるようです。元完璧主義者＆現完璧主義者の証言もそこら中にあって、非常に参考になります。僕だって、今までにも幾人ものエターナラーを見てきました。ＳＦＣの初代ツクールをいじっていた頃は自分自身も何度かエターなりましたので、多少の心理も分かります。幸い脱出に成功しましたが……。
blocks.translation: So I investigated the matter thoroughly. There seems to be a wealth of research on the psychology of perfectionists. Testimony from former and current perfectionists can be found everywhere, and it is extremely informative. I myself have seen many eternalizers over the years. When I was tinkering with the original RPG Maker on the SFC, I went eternal several times myself, so I have some understanding of the psychology involved. Fortunately, I managed to escape…

blocks.source: そういった調査結果を分析し、推論と検証を行うことで、かなりの答えを導き出すことができました。ゲーム制作という分野において、ここまで詳細なエターナルメカニズムを暴き出したのは、この記事が初めてではないでしょうか？
blocks.translation: By analyzing those research findings and conducting inference and verification, I was able to arrive at quite a few answers. In the field of game development, might this be the first article to expose the mechanism of going eternal in such detail?

blocks.source: ※若干、誇張がありますが分析自体はわりと真面目です。当ブログの過去の講座と比較しても、気合の入った記事となっています。
blocks.translation: ※This is slightly exaggerated, but the analysis itself is fairly serious. Compared with this blog's previous guides, this article is unusually ambitious.

blocks.source: なぜ完璧主義者はエターなるのか？
blocks.translation: Why Do Perfectionists Go Eternal?

blocks.source: まず、完璧主義者は細部までこだわって時間をかける傾向があります。これは予想通りですが、その結果、力尽きて作品を完成できないことが多いようなのです。
blocks.translation: First of all, perfectionists tend to spend a great deal of time attending to every detail. This is as expected, but as a result, they often run out of steam and fail to complete their work.

blocks.source: じゃあ、質を落としても作業を速めたらいいじゃないかと思うところですが……。曰く「１００％が無理なら、０％でも９０％でも大差ない」「下手なまま完成させたくない」というような思考をたどって、妥協するぐらいなら投げ出すという選択をしてしまうのです。
blocks.translation: You might think they should simply work faster, even if it means lowering the quality, but… They follow lines of thought such as “If 100% is impossible, then 0% and 90% are hardly any different” and “I don't want to finish it while it's still poorly made,” ultimately choosing to give up rather than compromise.

blocks.source: 完璧主義とは「完璧にする」ではなく「完璧にありたいと考える」であり、そのため「完璧にするのが困難ならば投げ出す」という行動も取るわけです。何かと完璧にしてきた人達は、それだけにその大変さを内心では理解しています。だからこそ『したい』とは考えても『する』とは限らないということですね。
blocks.translation: Perfectionism does not mean “making things perfect,” but “wanting things to be perfect.” Therefore, it can also lead to the behavior of “giving up if making something perfect is difficult.” People who have made everything perfect in one way or another understand inwardly just how difficult it is. That is why, even if they think “I want to,” it does not necessarily mean they will “do it.”

blocks.source: この投げ出すという性質によって、一見すると全く完璧に見えない人が完璧主義者だということもありえますので、注意してください。そのような、隠れ完璧主義についても上の性格診断やゲームのプレイスタイルを見れば判明する……はず。
blocks.translation: Please note that, because of this tendency to give up, someone who appears to be anything but perfect may actually be a perfectionist. Hidden perfectionism like this should also become apparent from the personality test above and their gaming style… at least in theory.

blocks.source: では、そもそも完璧主義者はなぜ完璧を目指すのでしょうか？ まず、思いつくのは『向上心』がそうさせているという考えです。実際そういう説明をしているところが多いですが、それにしては説明のつかない行動が散見されます。例えば「時間効率を軽視する」「価値の低いことに時間をかける」といった性質です。
blocks.translation: So why do perfectionists strive for perfection in the first place? The first explanation that comes to mind is that “a desire for self-improvement” drives them. Many sources do in fact explain it that way, but then we see various behaviors that cannot be explained by it, such as “disregarding time efficiency” and “spending time on things of little value.”

blocks.source: 向上心だけが理由ならば、これらも軽視できません。向上心もあるでしょうが、それだけでは説明不足です。
blocks.translation: If self-improvement were the only reason, these things could not be disregarded either. They may indeed have a desire for self-improvement, but that alone is not enough to explain it.

blocks.source: そこで、僕の出した推論は、完璧主義の方は『いらない物を捨てる判断が苦手』『自分で課題を決めるのが苦手』というように『決断』や『判断』そのものが苦手ではないかということです。
blocks.translation: This led me to the hypothesis that perfectionists may be poor at “decision-making” and “judgment” themselves—for example, they are “bad at deciding to throw away things they don't need” and “bad at setting goals for themselves.”

blocks.source: 捨てられないから、何でもかんでもやってしまう。
blocks.translation: Because they can't throw anything away, they try to do everything.

blocks.source: 自分で決められないから、外部から与えられた課題に飛びつく。なのに、本心からやりたいことではないのでモチベーションが低い。
blocks.translation: Because they can't decide for themselves, they seize upon tasks given to them from outside. Yet their motivation is low because these are not things they genuinely want to do.

blocks.source: 引き際の判断が苦手だから、楽しくないことでも１００％まで続けてしまう。
blocks.translation: Because they are bad at deciding when to quit, they continue even unenjoyable tasks until they reach 100%.

blocks.source: 要するに『度合』を決めるのが苦手だから、必然的に「最後までやる」か「早々に放り出す。または最初からやらない」になっていたという推論です。考えてみれば「７０％で切り上げる」という行為には意外と意志の力を要すものですから。
blocks.translation: In short, this is the hypothesis that because they are bad at deciding the “degree” of something, they inevitably either “see it through to the end” or “give up at an early stage—or never start in the first place.” When you think about it, stopping at 70% actually requires a surprising amount of willpower.

blocks.source: なぜ、判断や決断が苦手なのかというと、完璧主義の人は「人の期待に応える」「人の賞賛を受ける」ことの優先順位が高いからだそうです。相対的に「自分で考えて決める」「自分がやりたいことをやる」「やりたくないことはやらない」という意識が弱くなるわけです。
blocks.translation: Apparently, the reason they are bad at judgment and decision-making is that perfectionists place a high priority on “meeting other people's expectations” and “receiving other people's praise.” By comparison, they have a weaker awareness of “thinking and deciding for themselves,” “doing what they want to do,” and “not doing what they don't want to do.”

blocks.source: 人の期待に応えるために『結果』をモチベーションとすると、反面『結果のための過程』が苦行になりがちです。なんせ、ゲーム制作は長丁場ですから、制作過程を楽しめなければ、終わりのない苦行になってしまいます。
blocks.translation: When “the result” becomes the motivation for meeting other people's expectations, “the process required to achieve that result” tends to become an ordeal. After all, game development is a long-term undertaking. If you cannot enjoy the development process, it becomes an endless ordeal.

blocks.source: 他者の反響を意識する心理が強いことから、失敗を恐れる心理もまた強く働きます。その結果、意外にも『優柔不断』に陥りやすく「こんなに頑張ったのに不評だったらどうしよう。やっぱり作りなおしたほうが……」となって初志貫徹できずにエターなるというわけです。
blocks.translation: Because they are strongly focused on other people's reactions, their fear of failure also becomes more powerful. As a result, they are surprisingly prone to indecisiveness: “What if people dislike it after I've worked this hard? Maybe I should remake it after all…” And so they fail to follow through on their original intention and go eternal.

blocks.source: このような『失敗を避ける』という心理は、完璧主義ゲーマーのプレイスタイルとも一致しています。装備を完全に整えていれば、敵に負ける可能性は低くなるというわけです。
blocks.translation: This psychology of “avoiding failure” also matches the playing style of perfectionist gamers. If their equipment is fully prepared, they are less likely to lose to an enemy.

blocks.source: ですが、逆説的にそれは『失敗から学ぶ』機会の喪失も意味します。一般的なプレイヤーならば、敵が強くて負けた際に「このボスは力が強い。次は守備力を重視した戦術を試してみよう」というように、自然と失敗から学んで試行錯誤する経験を積むことになります。また、強敵相手に戦うには臨機応変な対応が必要ですから、自然と判断力を養えます。
blocks.translation: Paradoxically, however, this also means losing opportunities to “learn from failure.” When an ordinary player loses because an enemy is too strong, they naturally gain experience learning from failure and experimenting through trial and error, thinking, “This boss is powerful. Next time, I'll try a strategy that emphasizes defense.” Furthermore, fighting powerful enemies requires a flexible response, which naturally develops one's ability to make decisions.

blocks.source: これはゲームのプレイスタイルに限定したわけでもなく、普段の生活全般にもいえる話です。入念な準備をすると失敗は避けることができる。……が、同時に失敗した後の克服を学ぶ機会が減少します。
blocks.translation: This is not limited to gaming styles; it also applies to everyday life in general. Thorough preparation can help you avoid failure… but at the same time, it reduces opportunities to learn how to overcome failure afterward.

blocks.source: 完璧主義的なエターなる要因をまとめると……
blocks.translation: To summarize the perfectionism-related causes of going eternal…

blocks.source: ステップを無視した高すぎる目標意識。
blocks.translation: Excessively high goals that ignore the necessary steps.

blocks.source: 「よし、ＦＦ級の超大作ＲＰＧを作るぞ！
blocks.translation: "All right, I'm going to make an epic RPG on the scale of FF!

blocks.source: 一度も作品を完成させたことないけどイケるイケる！」
blocks.translation: I've never finished a project before, but I can totally do it!"

blocks.source: 質やこだわりを重視して、時間を顧みない。
blocks.translation: Prioritizing quality and attention to detail while disregarding the time involved.

blocks.source: 「ＦＦ級といえば当然フルボイスだな。
blocks.translation: "If it's on the scale of FF, it obviously needs full voice acting.

blocks.source: 今の内に俺もヴォイスの練習やっとくか！」
blocks.translation: I might as well start practicing my voice acting now!"

blocks.source: 判断力・決断力の不足。特に取捨選択が苦手。
blocks.translation: Insufficient judgment and decision-making ability, especially difficulty choosing what to keep and what to discard.

blocks.source: 「予定だと仲間が５０人を超えるな。
blocks.translation: "The plan has more than 50 party members.

blocks.source: 減らしたほうが……。いいや、全員出してしまえ！」
blocks.translation: Maybe I should reduce them… No, I'll include everyone!"

blocks.source: 自分がやりたいことより、他者からの反響を優先する。
blocks.translation: Prioritizing other people's reactions over what they themselves want to do.

blocks.source: 「これが完成したら、俺も有名クリエイターだな。
blocks.translation: "Once this is finished, I'll be a famous creator too.

blocks.source: きっと、女の子にもモテモテだぜ！」
blocks.translation: I'll be wildly popular with the girls!"

blocks.source: 過程を楽しめない結果偏重主義。
blocks.translation: An outcome-oriented mindset that cannot enjoy the process.

blocks.source: 「マップ制作とかストーリーとかスクリプトとかダルいな……。
blocks.translation: "Making maps, writing the story, and scripting are such a pain…

blocks.source: 誰か他の人がやってくんないかな……」
blocks.translation: I wish someone else would do it…"

blocks.source: 無謀な目標に真面目な性格が合わさった自己への過剰負担。
blocks.translation: Excessive self-imposed pressure caused by combining reckless goals with a serious personality.

blocks.source: 「徹夜で作業したからしんどい……。
blocks.translation: "I'm exhausted from working all night…

blocks.source: でも、これぐらい頑張らないと終わらないよな」
blocks.translation: But it won't get finished unless I work this hard."

blocks.source: 終わりが見えない作業への不安。
blocks.translation: Anxiety about work with no end in sight.

blocks.source: 「まだ、一割もできてない。いつになったら終わるんだろ……」
blocks.translation: "I haven't even finished 10% yet. I wonder when it will ever be done…"

blocks.source: 失敗への恐怖による優柔不断。
blocks.translation: Indecisiveness caused by fear of failure.

blocks.source: 「完成してもつまらないかも。
blocks.translation: "It might be boring even when it’s finished.

blocks.source: やっぱりアクションＲＰＧとして作りなおそうか……」
blocks.translation: Maybe I should remake it as an action RPG after all…"

blocks.source: 「」内は多少誇張してますが、こうしてみるとエターなる要因が満載ですね。能力や根気といった要因を除けば、エターナル要因をほぼ網羅している気すらします。
blocks.translation: The parts inside the quotation marks are somewhat exaggerated, but looking at it this way, they’re packed with reasons projects go eternally unfinished. Leaving aside factors such as ability and perseverance, they almost seem to cover every reason a project might never be completed.

blocks.source: 人間には個性があるし成長もするので、完璧主義傾向があるからといって、全部が全部当てはまるとは限りません。それぞれの根本は似たような心理かもしれませんが、個別に克服している方もいるでしょう。
blocks.translation: People have individual personalities and grow over time, so having perfectionist tendencies doesn’t necessarily mean that every single one of these applies. The underlying psychology may be similar in each case, but some people may have overcome them individually.

blocks.source: もし、全部当てはまったという方がいれば、相当な真正エターナラーです。天地がひっくり返っても完成することはないので、意識を改めましょう。
blocks.translation: If all of these apply to you, you’re a truly hardcore eternal-project person. Even if heaven and earth were turned upside down, you’d never finish anything, so it’s time to change your mindset.

blocks.source: 完璧主義を自覚しながらも、実際に作品を安定して完成できている方は、何かしらの柔軟性を持っているのだと思います。例えば「時間効率を考慮できる」「興味がないことは手を抜く」などです。
blocks.translation: Those who are aware of their perfectionism yet can consistently finish their projects in practice probably have some kind of flexibility. For example, they can take time efficiency into account or cut corners on things they aren’t interested in.

blocks.source: 柔軟性をあまり持たないまま、努力と能力でねじ伏せることによって、大作を完成させる方もたまに見かけますが、やはり負担が大きいようです。ユーザからの批判に敏感なことも合わさって、非常に疲れやすい傾向が見えます。あれでは「よし次の作品を作るぞ！」というモチベーションを起こすのは大変でしょうね。
blocks.translation: I occasionally see people complete major projects by overpowering everything with effort and ability despite lacking much flexibility, but it still seems to place a heavy burden on them. Combined with their sensitivity to criticism from users, they appear to be extremely prone to exhaustion. In that state, it must be difficult to summon the motivation to say, “All right, I’m going to make my next game!”

blocks.source: 以上の考察が正しければ、完璧主義がなぜエターなるのかが実によく分かります。というのも、話を聞けば、自分が作品を完成させる際に重視する点と一致しないからです。つまり、行動原理やモチベーションの持ち方が異なるということです。詳しく説明してみます。
blocks.translation: If the above analysis is correct, it becomes remarkably clear why perfectionists leave projects eternally unfinished. The reason is that, based on what I’ve heard, their priorities when completing a project don’t align with mine. In other words, their principles of action and sources of motivation are different. Let me explain in more detail.

blocks.source: 完璧主義が数々のエターナル要因を網羅するため、その対策も広く網羅したものになります。くしくも、完璧主義者に限らない多数のエターナラーに適用できるものになりましたので、皆様ご参考にください。
blocks.translation: Because perfectionism encompasses so many reasons projects go eternally unfinished, the countermeasures must also cover a broad range of issues. As it happens, they can be applied to many people who leave projects unfinished, not just perfectionists, so I hope everyone will find them useful.

blocks.source: エターならないために！
blocks.translation: How Not to Leave Projects Eternally Unfinished!

blocks.source: というわけで、僕が実践している方法を中心にエターナル対策を紹介していきます。意識してやっているものもあれば、自然とやっていたものもあります。ここでは制作意識の持ち方といった内容が中心になりますが、過去には具体的な制作技術を書いています。よろしければ、こちらもご参考にどうぞ。
blocks.translation: With that in mind, I’ll introduce ways to prevent projects from becoming eternal ones, focusing on the methods I practice. Some are things I do consciously, while others came naturally to me. This section mainly covers mindset during development, but I’ve written about specific development techniques in the past as well. Please feel free to refer to those too.

blocks.source: まず、モチベーションの持ち方ですが、僕は「下手から上手になっていく過程」が大好きなのです。人に見せるかどうかはともかく、途中の下手な成果物も記念碑として残しておきます。自分の成長が形として残るなんて最高です。
blocks.translation: First, regarding how I maintain my motivation: I love the process of going from being bad at something to becoming good at it. Whether or not I show them to others, I keep my mediocre early results as monuments. There’s nothing better than having my own growth remain in tangible form.

blocks.source: ドット絵をやったり、作曲をやったりとそれまで経験の薄かった分野にチャレンジするのも、この性質から来ています。できなかったことを努力して、できるようにするのが楽しいのです。だから、最初は下手でも気にしません。というか、下手じゃないと上達が実感できないので物足りません。
blocks.translation: This is also why I challenge myself in fields where I previously had little experience, such as pixel art and composing music. I enjoy working hard at things I couldn’t do until I become able to do them. So I don’t mind being bad at first. In fact, if I weren’t bad at first, I wouldn’t be able to feel myself improving, and it would feel unsatisfying.

blocks.source: 黒歴史ＲＰＧのリンクを貼っているのは、上達を実感できる記念碑だからでもあります。努力したらこんなに伸びるんだぞと。もっとも、あれだって何年か経験を積んだからこそできた作品ではありますが。
blocks.translation: One reason I link to my embarrassing RPG is that it serves as a monument to how much I’ve improved. It shows that hard work can take you this far. Of course, I was only able to make that game after gaining several years of experience.

blocks.source: というように自分の努力や成長を楽しみ、モチベーションとすることが第一です。ただし、色々と挑戦することまではそんなにお勧めしません。どちらかというとエターナル要因なので、好きな分野に絞って、後はフリー素材の活用等をお勧めします。
blocks.translation: So, first and foremost, enjoy your own efforts and growth, and use them as motivation. However, I don’t particularly recommend taking on challenges in lots of different areas. That tends to become a reason projects go eternally unfinished, so I recommend narrowing your focus to the fields you enjoy and making use of free assets for the rest.

blocks.source: 作品への時間のかけ方だけみると、僕も完璧主義っぽく見えるかもしれませんし、実際一種の完璧主義かもしれません。ただし、過去に２０以上の作品（ゴミのような短編含む）を完成させた上でやっています。これぐらいやらないと過去作品を越えられないというだけで、実際には少しづつ階段を登ってきています。
blocks.translation: Judging just by how much time I spend on my projects, I may look like a perfectionist too, and in fact I may be a kind of perfectionist. However, I’m doing this after having completed more than 20 projects in the past, including short games that were practically garbage. It’s not that I can’t surpass my past work without putting in this much effort; in reality, I’ve been climbing the stairs little by little.

blocks.source: 最初の頃に作った作品は出来が悪くて、本当に見せるに忍びないという感じになるかもしれませんが、その場合は無理して公開する必要もありません。身内向けのバカゲーを作って内輪に見せるだけでも全然ＯＫです。とにかく気楽に完成させてみるといいでしょう。
blocks.translation: The projects you make early on may turn out so poorly that you really can’t bear to show them to anyone, but in that case, you don’t need to force yourself to publish them. It’s perfectly fine to make a silly game for your friends and family and show it only to them. Above all, try finishing something without putting too much pressure on yourself.

blocks.source: 思えば、今の時代はプロ顔負けのフリゲが出回っていたりするので、比較して気後れしてしまうというのはあるかもしれませんね。「努力しても、こんな凄い作品に勝てるのか……？ 自分の作品に価値があるのか……？」と不安になるかもしれません。昔はそんな比較対象はありませんでしたから。
blocks.translation: Come to think of it, free games that rival professional titles are circulating nowadays, so it’s understandable if comparing yourself to them makes you feel intimidated. You may worry, “Even if I work hard, can I really compete with a game this amazing...? Does my own game have any value...?” There were no such points of comparison in the past.

blocks.source: ですが、そんな比較は疲れるだけです。見習うのはよいですが、仮想ライバルとするのは早すぎます。気にせず気楽に楽しみながら作っていればよいのです。その内、何作か完成させてみたら「おっ！」と思える作品ができあがります。自分なりの味みたいなものも出てくるので「他の作品にはない価値」を見出だせるようになってきます。
blocks.translation: However, comparisons like that will only wear you out. It’s fine to learn from them, but it’s too soon to treat them as imaginary rivals. Just keep making things casually and enjoying yourself without worrying about it. Eventually, after completing a few projects, you’ll create something that makes you think, “Oh!” You’ll also develop something like a style of your own, allowing you to discover “value that other works don’t have.”

blocks.source: そうして、自信ができたなら、初めて仮想ライバルを持つとよいかもしれません。おすすめは「自分よりちょっと上の人」です。時折、アマチュア評論家が出来の悪い市販ゲームに対して「こんなの俺でも作れる！」と豪語してたりしますが、そういう意識も悪くありません。「船頭多くして船山に上る」なんていう言葉もあって、アマチュアが大規模開発のプロより面白いものを作ることは珍しくありません。
blocks.translation: Once you’ve gained some confidence, you might consider finding an imaginary rival for the first time. I recommend choosing “someone just a little better than you.” Amateur critics sometimes boast about poorly made commercial games, saying, “I could make something like this!” That kind of attitude isn’t necessarily bad. There’s a saying that too many boatmen make the boat climb a mountain, and it’s not unusual for amateurs to create something more entertaining than professionals working on large-scale productions.

blocks.source: 話を戻して意識の持ち方です。僕の場合、目的意識なく物事を続けないように普段から心がけています。重要度が低いことは完璧を目指しません。得るものがないと判断すれば、スパッと見切りをつけて効率よくやりたいことに時間を注ぎます。本当に向上心があって完璧を目指すならば、こちらのほうがよっぽど理にかなっていると思ってます。
blocks.translation: Returning to the subject of mindset, I make a point of not continuing with things without a clear purpose. I don’t aim for perfection in matters of low importance. If I decide there’s nothing to gain, I cut my losses cleanly and devote my time to what I want to do efficiently. If you genuinely aspire to improve and aim for perfection, I think this approach makes far more sense.

blocks.source: もちろん、仕事は忙しくなければ真っ先に定時退社。
blocks.translation: Of course, if work isn’t busy, I’m the first one out the door at quitting time.

blocks.source: お陰様でリアルでドライ＆クールな人扱いですよ……。
blocks.translation: Thanks to that, people in real life treat me as a detached and cool person...

blocks.source: 睡眠だって、きっちり取ります。自分に負担をかけるようなやり方はどうせ長続きしませんので。
blocks.translation: I also make sure to get enough sleep. Any approach that puts too much strain on me wouldn’t last anyway.

blocks.source: そして行動原理。本音を言うと「人の期待に応える」なんて意識は最初から大して持っちゃいません。基本的には「自分がやりたいことをやる」というのが第一です。人に見せるのはあくまで第二です。快適性を重視するのは他者への配慮よりも、自分がプレイヤーとして快適にやりたいからです。
blocks.translation: And then there are my principles of action. To be honest, I’ve never really had much of a mindset of “meeting other people’s expectations” from the start. Basically, my first priority is “doing what I want to do.” Showing it to others comes second. I prioritize comfort not out of consideration for others, but because I want to enjoy the experience comfortably as a player myself.

blocks.source: そんな考え方で良いのかというと、良いのです。自分が楽しめる作品を作れば、人が楽しめる作品も自然とできあがるもの。Win-Winの関係というやつですね。感性が合わない人ももちろんいますが、世の中には色んな人がいるのだから、気にしてもきりがありません。
blocks.translation: Is it really okay to think that way? Yes, it is. If you make something you can enjoy, something other people can enjoy will naturally emerge as well. That’s what you call a win-win relationship. Of course, there will be people whose sensibilities don’t match yours, but there are all kinds of people in the world, so worrying about it is pointless.

blocks.source: てな感じで、完璧主義が原因で作品を完成できない、という人は意識を変えてみるとよいかもしれません。このタイプは努力家という最高の才能を持っているわりに、それが空回りしてしまう。結果、高い理想と現実のギャップに苦しむという損な人が多そうです。
blocks.translation: So, if you’re someone who can’t finish projects because of perfectionism, it may be worth changing your mindset. Although this type of person possesses the superb talent of being hardworking, that effort often ends up spinning its wheels. As a result, many of them seem to suffer from the gap between their lofty ideals and reality.

blocks.source: ですが、それだけに柔軟性を手に入れて、作品を完成させることを積み重ねていけば相当良い線いけるんじゃないかと思います。
blocks.translation: But precisely because of that, I think they could go a long way if they acquired some flexibility and kept building a track record of finishing their projects.

blocks.source: そして、完璧主義の方はネガティブなスパイラルに陥りやすいとのこと。挫折が続くと「自分には才能がない。努力したって無駄だ」なんて思考の落とし穴に陥りがちです。
blocks.translation: I’ve also heard that perfectionists are prone to falling into a negative spiral. When setbacks continue, they tend to fall into the mental trap of thinking, “I have no talent. There’s no point in working hard.”

blocks.source: しかし、才能ってものは『有』か『無』かのようなそんな単純なものではありません。僕も色んな作品をやってきましたが「この作者は才能がない。努力したって無駄だ」なんて思ったことは一度足りともありません。
blocks.translation: However, talent isn’t something as simple as having it or not having it. I’ve worked on all kinds of projects, but I’ve never once thought, “This creator has no talent. There’s no point in working hard.”

blocks.source: もちろん、つまらない作品もありますが、その場合もつまらない理由があります。大抵は「物語が平坦」「テンポが悪い」「システムが無駄に複雑」みたいに明確です。理由があるということは改善できるということです。
blocks.translation: Of course, some projects are boring, but there’s always a reason they’re boring. Usually, it’s something clear, such as “the story is flat,” “the pacing is poor,” or “the system is unnecessarily complicated.” If there’s a reason, it can be improved.

blocks.source: ロクに努力したことがない人間ほど「才能がない人間は努力したって無駄だ」みたいなことを安直に言いますが、気にすることはありません。努力したことがない人間には「努力したら人間は伸びる」という当たり前のことが理解できないのです。
blocks.translation: People who have barely made any effort are the ones who casually say things like, “There’s no point in working hard if you lack talent,” but you shouldn’t let it bother you. People who have never made an effort can’t understand the obvious fact that people improve when they work hard.

blocks.source: 僕は努力厨なので「自分が努力することで伸びた」ということをはっきりと把握しています。でもって、分析厨なので人の作品を見ると、改善できる点がワラワラ浮かんできます。もし、改善できる点が浮かばないとしたら、それは本当に完璧なので僕には指摘できないというだけです。
blocks.translation: I’m something of an effort fanatic, so I clearly understand that “I improved by working hard.” And since I’m also an analysis fanatic, when I look at other people’s work, points that could be improved come pouring into my mind. If no points for improvement come to mind, it simply means the work is genuinely perfect and I have nothing to point out.

blocks.source: 改善できる余地があるということは、努力する余地もあるということ。「努力したって無駄」なんて結論にはなりません。逆に言えば、本当の意味で才能がないといえるのは「努力しない」「学ばない」「挑戦しない」人達です。
blocks.translation: The fact that there’s room for improvement means there’s also room for effort. You can’t conclude that “working hard is pointless.” Conversely, the people who can truly be said to lack talent are those who don’t make an effort, don’t learn, and don’t take on challenges.

blocks.source: もっとも「努力したら夢が叶うのか？」といったことまでは保証できません。保証できるのは「努力したら夢に近づく」ということまでです。
blocks.translation: That said, I can’t guarantee that working hard will make your dreams come true. What I can guarantee is that working hard will bring you closer to your dreams.

blocks.source: ですが、そもそも『叶う』『叶わない』という二者択一自体が柔軟性を欠いた完璧主義思考といえます。その夢は本当に１００％叶えなければ駄目なのでしょうか。１％でも叶えたならば、０％よりはマシだと思いませんか？
blocks.translation: However, the very either-or choice between “coming true” and “not coming true” is a perfectionist way of thinking that lacks flexibility. Does that dream really have to come true 100 percent? If you make it come true even by 1 percent, wouldn’t that be better than 0 percent?

blocks.source: 例えば、漫画家になりたいという夢だと……
blocks.translation: For example, suppose your dream is to become a manga artist...

blocks.source: 有名誌に連載して大ヒット。億万長者。
blocks.translation: A series in a famous magazine becomes a huge hit. You become a multimillionaire.

blocks.source: マイナー誌で連載して小ヒット。生活できる程度の給与をもらう。
blocks.translation: A series in a minor magazine becomes a modest hit. You earn enough to live on.

blocks.source: 副業として同人誌を出して小遣い稼ぎ。
blocks.translation: You publish self-published comics as a side job and earn some pocket money.

blocks.source: 趣味としてWeb上に無料公開して、ちょっとした人気を得る。
blocks.translation: You publish your work for free online as a hobby and gain a little popularity.

blocks.source: 身内に見せてウケを取る。
blocks.translation: You show it to your friends and family and get some laughs.

blocks.source: というように色々とあります。『１』を達成しなければ意味がない、なんて理由はあるでしょうか？ 『３』でも達成できたならば儲けものですし、その後で『１』や『２』を狙うことも十分可能です。『１』じゃなければ駄目だというならば、そもそも漫画を描くこと自体がさして好きでないのでは、となりますよね。
blocks.translation: There are various possibilities like these. Is there really any reason why it would be meaningless unless you achieve “1”? If you can achieve “3,” that’s already a gain, and you can still aim for “1” or “2” afterward. If anything but “1” isn’t good enough, then perhaps you don’t really like drawing manga that much in the first place, right?

blocks.source: 『４』や『５』では利益がないから意味がないという人もいるかもしれません。でも、せっかく空いた時間があるなら、好きなことに時間を使いたくありませんか？ 特に「仕事がつまらない」なんて人は何もしなかったら「人生がつまらない」にまっしぐらです。
blocks.translation: Some people may say that “4” and “5” are meaningless because they bring no profit. But if you have free time, wouldn’t you rather spend it doing something you enjoy? In particular, people who say “work is boring” will be heading straight toward “life is boring” if they do nothing.

blocks.source: 以上。……こんなに頑張って記事を書いたのは久しぶりです。期せずして「人はなぜエターなるのか？」という永遠の命題にかなり迫れたような気がしたので、湧き上がるものがありました。内容が長すぎて混沌としているのでこの記事は今後ともちょくちょく整理するかもしれません。
blocks.translation: That’s all. ...It’s been a long time since I worked this hard on an article. I unexpectedly felt inspired because I think I’ve come quite close to the eternal question, “Why do people leave projects eternally unfinished?” The article is so long and chaotic that I may organize it from time to time in the future.

lines.source: 課題を立てて徐々にステップアップすることを知らず、いきなり無謀な目標を意識して挫折する。（[[LINK_1]]例[[/LINK_1]]）

parts.source: 課題を立てて徐々にステップアップすることを知らず、いきなり無謀な目標を意識して挫折する。（

lines.translation: They do not know how to set tasks and gradually step up, and instead become fixated on an unreasonable goal from the start and give up. ([[LINK_1]]Example[[/LINK_1]])

texts.さて、前編で終わるつもりだったのですが、そうはいきませんでした。極めて重大な情報: Well, I intended to wrap things up in the first part, but that didn't happen. I came across some extremely important information. It was this…
texts.完璧主義者はエターなりやすいということです。: Perfectionists are prone to going eternal.
texts.※エターなる：作品を制作途中で放棄することの意。: ※Going eternal: Abandoning a work while it is still in production.
texts.……この情報には僕も驚愕を隠せません。完璧主義者はプレイヤーとしては、アイテムコ: …I can't hide my astonishment at this information either. As players, perfectionists have the disposition to complete painstaking tasks such as collecting every item. Since they possess considerable perseverance, I had thought they were, if anything, the type who could finish things.
texts.それがなぜ、エターなるというのか？ これは「人はなぜエターなるのか？」という命題: Why, then, do they go eternal? As someone who has pursued the question “Why do people go eternal?”, I can't overlook this. It would not be an exaggeration to say that unraveling the mechanism of going eternal and rescuing as many eternalizers as possible from the sea of eternity is the supreme mission of [RPG Design Guides] .
texts.というわけで、徹底調査しました。完璧主義者の心理についてはかなり豊富な調査結果が: So I investigated the matter thoroughly. There seems to be a wealth of research on the psychology of perfectionists. Testimony from former and current perfectionists can be found everywhere, and it is extremely informative. I myself have seen many eternalizers over the years. When I was tinkering with the original RPG Maker on the SFC, I went eternal several times myself, so I have some understanding of the psychology involved. Fortunately, I managed to escape…
texts.そういった調査結果を分析し、推論と検証を行うことで、かなりの答えを導き出すことが: By analyzing those research findings and conducting inference and verification, I was able to arrive at quite a few answers. In the field of game development, might this be the first article to expose the mechanism of going eternal in such detail?
texts.※若干、誇張がありますが分析自体はわりと真面目です。当ブログの過去の講座と比較し: ※This is slightly exaggerated, but the analysis itself is fairly serious. Compared with this blog's previous guides, this article is unusually ambitious.
texts.まず、完璧主義者は細部までこだわって時間をかける傾向があります。これは予想通りで: First of all, perfectionists tend to spend a great deal of time attending to every detail. This is as expected, but as a result, they often run out of steam and fail to complete their work.
texts.じゃあ、質を落としても作業を速めたらいいじゃないかと思うところですが……。曰く「: You might think they should simply work faster, even if it means lowering the quality, but… They follow lines of thought such as “If 100% is impossible, then 0% and 90% are hardly any different” and “I don't want to finish it while it's still poorly made,” ultimately choosing to give up rather than compromise.
texts.完璧主義とは「完璧にする」ではなく「完璧にありたいと考える」であり、そのため「完: Perfectionism does not mean “making things perfect,” but “wanting things to be perfect.” Therefore, it can also lead to the behavior of “giving up if making something perfect is difficult.” People who have made everything perfect in one way or another understand inwardly just how difficult it is. That is why, even if they think “I want to,” it does not necessarily mean they will “do it.”
texts.この投げ出すという性質によって、一見すると全く完璧に見えない人が完璧主義者だとい: Please note that, because of this tendency to give up, someone who appears to be anything but perfect may actually be a perfectionist. Hidden perfectionism like this should also become apparent from the personality test above and their gaming style… at least in theory.
texts.では、そもそも完璧主義者はなぜ完璧を目指すのでしょうか？ まず、思いつくのは『向: So why do perfectionists strive for perfection in the first place? The first explanation that comes to mind is that “a desire for self-improvement” drives them. Many sources do in fact explain it that way, but then we see various behaviors that cannot be explained by it, such as “disregarding time efficiency” and “spending time on things of little value.”
texts.向上心だけが理由ならば、これらも軽視できません。向上心もあるでしょうが、それだけ: If self-improvement were the only reason, these things could not be disregarded either. They may indeed have a desire for self-improvement, but that alone is not enough to explain it.
texts.そこで、僕の出した推論は、完璧主義の方は『いらない物を捨てる判断が苦手』『自分で: This led me to the hypothesis that perfectionists may be poor at “decision-making” and “judgment” themselves—for example, they are “bad at deciding to throw away things they don't need” and “bad at setting goals for themselves.”
texts.捨てられないから、何でもかんでもやってしまう。: Because they can't throw anything away, they try to do everything.
texts.自分で決められないから、外部から与えられた課題に飛びつく。なのに、本心からやりた: Because they can't decide for themselves, they seize upon tasks given to them from outside. Yet their motivation is low because these are not things they genuinely want to do.
texts.引き際の判断が苦手だから、楽しくないことでも１００％まで続けてしまう。: Because they are bad at deciding when to quit, they continue even unenjoyable tasks until they reach 100%.
texts.要するに『度合』を決めるのが苦手だから、必然的に「最後までやる」か「早々に放り出: In short, this is the hypothesis that because they are bad at deciding the “degree” of something, they inevitably either “see it through to the end” or “give up at an early stage—or never start in the first place.” When you think about it, stopping at 70% actually requires a surprising amount of willpower.
texts.なぜ、判断や決断が苦手なのかというと、完璧主義の人は「人の期待に応える」「人の賞: Apparently, the reason they are bad at judgment and decision-making is that perfectionists place a high priority on “meeting other people's expectations” and “receiving other people's praise.” By comparison, they have a weaker awareness of “thinking and deciding for themselves,” “doing what they want to do,” and “not doing what they don't want to do.”
texts.人の期待に応えるために『結果』をモチベーションとすると、反面『結果のための過程』: When “the result” becomes the motivation for meeting other people's expectations, “the process required to achieve that result” tends to become an ordeal. After all, game development is a long-term undertaking. If you cannot enjoy the development process, it becomes an endless ordeal.
texts.他者の反響を意識する心理が強いことから、失敗を恐れる心理もまた強く働きます。その: Because they are strongly focused on other people's reactions, their fear of failure also becomes more powerful. As a result, they are surprisingly prone to indecisiveness: “What if people dislike it after I've worked this hard? Maybe I should remake it after all…” And so they fail to follow through on their original intention and go eternal.
texts.このような『失敗を避ける』という心理は、完璧主義ゲーマーのプレイスタイルとも一致: This psychology of “avoiding failure” also matches the playing style of perfectionist gamers. If their equipment is fully prepared, they are less likely to lose to an enemy.
texts.ですが、逆説的にそれは『失敗から学ぶ』機会の喪失も意味します。一般的なプレイヤー: Paradoxically, however, this also means losing opportunities to “learn from failure.” When an ordinary player loses because an enemy is too strong, they naturally gain experience learning from failure and experimenting through trial and error, thinking, “This boss is powerful. Next time, I'll try a strategy that emphasizes defense.” Furthermore, fighting powerful enemies requires a flexible response, which naturally develops one's ability to make decisions.
texts.これはゲームのプレイスタイルに限定したわけでもなく、普段の生活全般にもいえる話で: This is not limited to gaming styles; it also applies to everyday life in general. Thorough preparation can help you avoid failure… but at the same time, it reduces opportunities to learn how to overcome failure afterward.
texts.完璧主義的なエターなる要因をまとめると……: To summarize the perfectionism-related causes of going eternal…
texts.ステップを無視した高すぎる目標意識。: Excessively high goals that ignore the necessary steps.
texts.「よし、ＦＦ級の超大作ＲＰＧを作るぞ！: "All right, I'm going to make an epic RPG on the scale of FF!
texts.一度も作品を完成させたことないけどイケるイケる！」: I've never finished a project before, but I can totally do it!"
texts.質やこだわりを重視して、時間を顧みない。: Prioritizing quality and attention to detail while disregarding the time involved.
texts.「ＦＦ級といえば当然フルボイスだな。: "If it's on the scale of FF, it obviously needs full voice acting.
texts.今の内に俺もヴォイスの練習やっとくか！」: I might as well start practicing my voice acting now!"
texts.判断力・決断力の不足。特に取捨選択が苦手。: Insufficient judgment and decision-making ability, especially difficulty choosing what to keep and what to discard.
texts.「予定だと仲間が５０人を超えるな。: "The plan has more than 50 party members.
texts.減らしたほうが……。いいや、全員出してしまえ！」: Maybe I should reduce them… No, I'll include everyone!"
texts.自分がやりたいことより、他者からの反響を優先する。: Prioritizing other people's reactions over what they themselves want to do.
texts.「これが完成したら、俺も有名クリエイターだな。: "Once this is finished, I'll be a famous creator too.
texts.きっと、女の子にもモテモテだぜ！」: I'll be wildly popular with the girls!"
texts.過程を楽しめない結果偏重主義。: An outcome-oriented mindset that cannot enjoy the process.
texts.「マップ制作とかストーリーとかスクリプトとかダルいな……。: "Making maps, writing the story, and scripting are such a pain…
texts.誰か他の人がやってくんないかな……」: I wish someone else would do it…"
texts.無謀な目標に真面目な性格が合わさった自己への過剰負担。: Excessive self-imposed pressure caused by combining reckless goals with a serious personality.
texts.でも、これぐらい頑張らないと終わらないよな」: But it won't get finished unless I work this hard."
texts.終わりが見えない作業への不安。: Anxiety about work with no end in sight.
texts.「まだ、一割もできてない。いつになったら終わるんだろ……」: "I haven't even finished 10% yet. I wonder when it will ever be done…"
texts.失敗への恐怖による優柔不断。: Indecisiveness caused by fear of failure.
texts.「完成してもつまらないかも。: "It might be boring even when it’s finished.
texts.やっぱりアクションＲＰＧとして作りなおそうか……」: Maybe I should remake it as an action RPG after all…"
texts.「」内は多少誇張してますが、こうしてみるとエターなる要因が満載ですね。能力や根気: The parts inside the quotation marks are somewhat exaggerated, but looking at it this way, they’re packed with reasons projects go eternally unfinished. Leaving aside factors such as ability and perseverance, they almost seem to cover every reason a project might never be completed.
texts.人間には個性があるし成長もするので、完璧主義傾向があるからといって、全部が全部当: People have individual personalities and grow over time, so having perfectionist tendencies doesn’t necessarily mean that every single one of these applies. The underlying psychology may be similar in each case, but some people may have overcome them individually.
texts.もし、全部当てはまったという方がいれば、相当な真正エターナラーです。天地がひっく: If all of these apply to you, you’re a truly hardcore eternal-project person. Even if heaven and earth were turned upside down, you’d never finish anything, so it’s time to change your mindset.
texts.完璧主義を自覚しながらも、実際に作品を安定して完成できている方は、何かしらの柔軟: Those who are aware of their perfectionism yet can consistently finish their projects in practice probably have some kind of flexibility. For example, they can take time efficiency into account or cut corners on things they aren’t interested in.
texts.柔軟性をあまり持たないまま、努力と能力でねじ伏せることによって、大作を完成させる: I occasionally see people complete major projects by overpowering everything with effort and ability despite lacking much flexibility, but it still seems to place a heavy burden on them. Combined with their sensitivity to criticism from users, they appear to be extremely prone to exhaustion. In that state, it must be difficult to summon the motivation to say, “All right, I’m going to make my next game!”
texts.以上の考察が正しければ、完璧主義がなぜエターなるのかが実によく分かります。という: If the above analysis is correct, it becomes remarkably clear why perfectionists leave projects eternally unfinished. The reason is that, based on what I’ve heard, their priorities when completing a project don’t align with mine. In other words, their principles of action and sources of motivation are different. Let me explain in more detail.
texts.完璧主義が数々のエターナル要因を網羅するため、その対策も広く網羅したものになりま: Because perfectionism encompasses so many reasons projects go eternally unfinished, the countermeasures must also cover a broad range of issues. As it happens, they can be applied to many people who leave projects unfinished, not just perfectionists, so I hope everyone will find them useful.
texts.エターならないために！: How Not to Leave Projects Eternally Unfinished!
texts.というわけで、僕が実践している方法を中心にエターナル対策を紹介していきます。意識: With that in mind, I’ll introduce ways to prevent projects from becoming eternal ones, focusing on the methods I practice. Some are things I do consciously, while others came naturally to me. This section mainly covers mindset during development, but I’ve written about specific development techniques in the past as well. Please feel free to refer to those too.
texts.まず、モチベーションの持ち方ですが、僕は「下手から上手になっていく過程」が大好き: First, regarding how I maintain my motivation: I love the process of going from being bad at something to becoming good at it. Whether or not I show them to others, I keep my mediocre early results as monuments. There’s nothing better than having my own growth remain in tangible form.
texts.ドット絵をやったり、作曲をやったりとそれまで経験の薄かった分野にチャレンジするの: This is also why I challenge myself in fields where I previously had little experience, such as pixel art and composing music. I enjoy working hard at things I couldn’t do until I become able to do them. So I don’t mind being bad at first. In fact, if I weren’t bad at first, I wouldn’t be able to feel myself improving, and it would feel unsatisfying.
texts.黒歴史ＲＰＧのリンクを貼っているのは、上達を実感できる記念碑だからでもあります。: One reason I link to my embarrassing RPG is that it serves as a monument to how much I’ve improved. It shows that hard work can take you this far. Of course, I was only able to make that game after gaining several years of experience.
texts.というように自分の努力や成長を楽しみ、モチベーションとすることが第一です。ただし: So, first and foremost, enjoy your own efforts and growth, and use them as motivation. However, I don’t particularly recommend taking on challenges in lots of different areas. That tends to become a reason projects go eternally unfinished, so I recommend narrowing your focus to the fields you enjoy and making use of free assets for the rest.
texts.作品への時間のかけ方だけみると、僕も完璧主義っぽく見えるかもしれませんし、実際一: Judging just by how much time I spend on my projects, I may look like a perfectionist too, and in fact I may be a kind of perfectionist. However, I’m doing this after having completed more than 20 projects in the past, including short games that were practically garbage. It’s not that I can’t surpass my past work without putting in this much effort; in reality, I’ve been climbing the stairs little by little.
texts.最初の頃に作った作品は出来が悪くて、本当に見せるに忍びないという感じになるかもし: The projects you make early on may turn out so poorly that you really can’t bear to show them to anyone, but in that case, you don’t need to force yourself to publish them. It’s perfectly fine to make a silly game for your friends and family and show it only to them. Above all, try finishing something without putting too much pressure on yourself.
texts.思えば、今の時代はプロ顔負けのフリゲが出回っていたりするので、比較して気後れして: Come to think of it, free games that rival professional titles are circulating nowadays, so it’s understandable if comparing yourself to them makes you feel intimidated. You may worry, “Even if I work hard, can I really compete with a game this amazing...? Does my own game have any value...?” There were no such points of comparison in the past.
texts.ですが、そんな比較は疲れるだけです。見習うのはよいですが、仮想ライバルとするのは: However, comparisons like that will only wear you out. It’s fine to learn from them, but it’s too soon to treat them as imaginary rivals. Just keep making things casually and enjoying yourself without worrying about it. Eventually, after completing a few projects, you’ll create something that makes you think, “Oh!” You’ll also develop something like a style of your own, allowing you to discover “value that other works don’t have.”
texts.そうして、自信ができたなら、初めて仮想ライバルを持つとよいかもしれません。おすす: Once you’ve gained some confidence, you might consider finding an imaginary rival for the first time. I recommend choosing “someone just a little better than you.” Amateur critics sometimes boast about poorly made commercial games, saying, “I could make something like this!” That kind of attitude isn’t necessarily bad. There’s a saying that too many boatmen make the boat climb a mountain, and it’s not unusual for amateurs to create something more entertaining than professionals working on large-scale productions.
texts.話を戻して意識の持ち方です。僕の場合、目的意識なく物事を続けないように普段から心: Returning to the subject of mindset, I make a point of not continuing with things without a clear purpose. I don’t aim for perfection in matters of low importance. If I decide there’s nothing to gain, I cut my losses cleanly and devote my time to what I want to do efficiently. If you genuinely aspire to improve and aim for perfection, I think this approach makes far more sense.
texts.もちろん、仕事は忙しくなければ真っ先に定時退社。: Of course, if work isn’t busy, I’m the first one out the door at quitting time.
texts.お陰様でリアルでドライ＆クールな人扱いですよ……。: Thanks to that, people in real life treat me as a detached and cool person...
texts.睡眠だって、きっちり取ります。自分に負担をかけるようなやり方はどうせ長続きしませ: I also make sure to get enough sleep. Any approach that puts too much strain on me wouldn’t last anyway.
texts.そして行動原理。本音を言うと「人の期待に応える」なんて意識は最初から大して持っち: And then there are my principles of action. To be honest, I’ve never really had much of a mindset of “meeting other people’s expectations” from the start. Basically, my first priority is “doing what I want to do.” Showing it to others comes second. I prioritize comfort not out of consideration for others, but because I want to enjoy the experience comfortably as a player myself.
texts.そんな考え方で良いのかというと、良いのです。自分が楽しめる作品を作れば、人が楽し: Is it really okay to think that way? Yes, it is. If you make something you can enjoy, something other people can enjoy will naturally emerge as well. That’s what you call a win-win relationship. Of course, there will be people whose sensibilities don’t match yours, but there are all kinds of people in the world, so worrying about it is pointless.
texts.てな感じで、完璧主義が原因で作品を完成できない、という人は意識を変えてみるとよい: So, if you’re someone who can’t finish projects because of perfectionism, it may be worth changing your mindset. Although this type of person possesses the superb talent of being hardworking, that effort often ends up spinning its wheels. As a result, many of them seem to suffer from the gap between their lofty ideals and reality.
texts.ですが、それだけに柔軟性を手に入れて、作品を完成させることを積み重ねていけば相当: But precisely because of that, I think they could go a long way if they acquired some flexibility and kept building a track record of finishing their projects.
texts.そして、完璧主義の方はネガティブなスパイラルに陥りやすいとのこと。挫折が続くと「: I’ve also heard that perfectionists are prone to falling into a negative spiral. When setbacks continue, they tend to fall into the mental trap of thinking, “I have no talent. There’s no point in working hard.”
texts.しかし、才能ってものは『有』か『無』かのようなそんな単純なものではありません。僕: However, talent isn’t something as simple as having it or not having it. I’ve worked on all kinds of projects, but I’ve never once thought, “This creator has no talent. There’s no point in working hard.”
texts.もちろん、つまらない作品もありますが、その場合もつまらない理由があります。大抵は: Of course, some projects are boring, but there’s always a reason they’re boring. Usually, it’s something clear, such as “the story is flat,” “the pacing is poor,” or “the system is unnecessarily complicated.” If there’s a reason, it can be improved.
texts.ロクに努力したことがない人間ほど「才能がない人間は努力したって無駄だ」みたいなこ: People who have barely made any effort are the ones who casually say things like, “There’s no point in working hard if you lack talent,” but you shouldn’t let it bother you. People who have never made an effort can’t understand the obvious fact that people improve when they work hard.
texts.僕は努力厨なので「自分が努力することで伸びた」ということをはっきりと把握していま: I’m something of an effort fanatic, so I clearly understand that “I improved by working hard.” And since I’m also an analysis fanatic, when I look at other people’s work, points that could be improved come pouring into my mind. If no points for improvement come to mind, it simply means the work is genuinely perfect and I have nothing to point out.
texts.改善できる余地があるということは、努力する余地もあるということ。「努力したって無: The fact that there’s room for improvement means there’s also room for effort. You can’t conclude that “working hard is pointless.” Conversely, the people who can truly be said to lack talent are those who don’t make an effort, don’t learn, and don’t take on challenges.
texts.もっとも「努力したら夢が叶うのか？」といったことまでは保証できません。保証できる: That said, I can’t guarantee that working hard will make your dreams come true. What I can guarantee is that working hard will bring you closer to your dreams.
texts.ですが、そもそも『叶う』『叶わない』という二者択一自体が柔軟性を欠いた完璧主義思: However, the very either-or choice between “coming true” and “not coming true” is a perfectionist way of thinking that lacks flexibility. Does that dream really have to come true 100 percent? If you make it come true even by 1 percent, wouldn’t that be better than 0 percent?
texts.例えば、漫画家になりたいという夢だと……: For example, suppose your dream is to become a manga artist...
texts.有名誌に連載して大ヒット。億万長者。: A series in a famous magazine becomes a huge hit. You become a multimillionaire.
texts.マイナー誌で連載して小ヒット。生活できる程度の給与をもらう。: A series in a minor magazine becomes a modest hit. You earn enough to live on.
texts.副業として同人誌を出して小遣い稼ぎ。: You publish self-published comics as a side job and earn some pocket money.
texts.趣味としてWeb上に無料公開して、ちょっとした人気を得る。: You publish your work for free online as a hobby and gain a little popularity.
texts.身内に見せてウケを取る。: You show it to your friends and family and get some laughs.
texts.というように色々とあります。『１』を達成しなければ意味がない、なんて理由はあるで: There are various possibilities like these. Is there really any reason why it would be meaningless unless you achieve “1”? If you can achieve “3,” that’s already a gain, and you can still aim for “1” or “2” afterward. If anything but “1” isn’t good enough, then perhaps you don’t really like drawing manga that much in the first place, right?
texts.『４』や『５』では利益がないから意味がないという人もいるかもしれません。でも、せ: Some people may say that “4” and “5” are meaningless because they bring no profit. But if you have free time, wouldn’t you rather spend it doing something you enjoy? In particular, people who say “work is boring” will be heading straight toward “life is boring” if they do nothing.

I unexpectedly felt inspired because I think I’ve come quite close to the eternal question, “Why do people leave projects eternally unfinished?” The article is so long and chaotic that I may organize it from time to time in the future.
